record.paper: Graphs with arbitrary Ramsey number and connectivity

dossier_meta.paper: Graphs with arbitrary Ramsey number and connectivity
dossier_meta.statement_text: For all functions $f(n) : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $n \leq f(n) \leq r(K_n)$ and for all $\varepsilon > 0$, there is a sequence of graphs $(G_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ satisfying $|V(G_n)| = n$ and $(1-\varepsilon)f(n) \leq r(G_n) \leq (1+\varepsilon)f(n)$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
dossier_meta.context_text: The paper's main theorem achieves every growth rate up to a multiplicative constant $C_k$; Conjecture 10 asks whether the multiplicative gaps in $\mathcal{R}^c_n$ can be made $1+o(1)$, i.e., whether any prescribed growth rate can be approximated arbitrarily closely. The authors suggest that edge-deletion results (such as a conjecture of Wigderson) might provide a route to this.
